title: Ciscomani welcomes continued federal funding for Arizona schools
text:
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | ciscomani.house.gov
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | ciscomani.house.gov
U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani has welcomed the continued release of federal funds aimed at supporting educational programs in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District. The funding will benefit English learners, teacher professional development, adult education, and after-school and summer learning opportunities for K-12 students.
“As a father of six and a proud product of public schools myself, I’ve seen how important it is to invest in strong educational support systems — from helping students learn English, to giving teachers the training they need to grow, to offering adult learners a second chance at success, and making sure kids have safe, enriching options after school and during the summer,” said Ciscomani. “After hearing directly from school leaders in our communities, I worked closely with the White House to secure funding for these essential programs that make a real difference for students, families, and educators.”
Ciscomani collaborated with local public school leaders and the White House to help ensure ongoing funding for key education initiatives such as Title I-C, II-A, II WIOA, III-A, IV-A, and 21st Century Community Learning Centers. This comes following a recent review by the Department of Education.
He also engaged with educators and organizations like the Boys & Girls Club to discuss the significance of these programs throughout his district.
The released funds are intended to provide resources for English language acquisition efforts, teacher development programs, adult education services, as well as after-school and summer activities.
Juan Ciscomani currently serves in Congress representing Arizona’s 6th district. He succeeded Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023 (https://www.congress.gov/member/juan-ciscomani/C001132). In previous elections—2022 and 2024—he won against Kirsten Engel (https://ballotpedia.org/Juan_Ciscomani).
